ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in square $ABCD$, $AB = 8\,cm$. Extend $BC$ to point $E$ so that $CE = 2\,cm$. Connect $DE$. A moving point $P$ starts from point $A$ and moves to the endpoint $A$ at a velocity of $2\,cm/s$, along the path $AB \rightarrow BC \rightarrow CD \rightarrow DA$. Let the movement time of point $P$ be $t$ seconds. When $\triangle PBC$ and $\triangle DCE$ are congruent, what is the value of $t$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure A, when $\triangle CBP_{1} \cong \triangle DCE$, we have $BP_{1} = CE = 2\text{cm}$, \\
thus $8-2t=2$. Solving for $t$ gives $t=\boxed{3}$, \\
As shown in Figure B, when $\triangle BCP_{2} \cong \triangle DCE$, we have $CP_{2} = CE=2\text{cm}$\\
thus $2t-2\times 8=2$. Solving for $t$ gives $t=9$.

For 0≤t≤4, P is on AB at (0,8-2t), so triangle PBC has sides BC=8, PB=8-2t, PC=sqrt(64+(8-2t)^2); matching the set {8,2,sqrt68} gives PB=2, hence t=3. For 4≤t≤8, P lies on BC, so triangle PBC is degenerate and cannot be congruent to DCE. For 8≤t≤12, P is on CD at (8,2t-16), so CP=2t-16 and matching the side set gives CP=2, hence t=9. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in square $ABCD$, $AB=8\,\text{cm}$. Extend $BC$ to point $E$ so that $CE=2\,\text{cm}$. Connect $DE$. A moving point $P$ starts from point $A$ and moves back to point $A$ at a velocity of $2\,\text{cm/s}$ along the path $AB \rightarrow BC \rightarrow CD \rightarrow DA$. Let the movement time of point $P$ be $t$ seconds. When $\triangle PBC$ and $\triangle DCE$ are congruent, what is the value of $t$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: As shown in Figure A, when $\triangle CBP_{1} \cong \triangle DCE$, we have $BP_{1}=CE=2\,\text{cm}$, so $8-2t=2$, giving $t=3$. As shown in Figure B, when $\triangle BCP_{2} \cong \triangle DCE$, we have $CP_{2}=CE=2\,\text{cm}$, so $2t-2\times 8=2$, giving $t=9$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, ABCD is a square, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right; BC is the horizontal bottom side, and CD is the vertical right side; E is located to the right of C, on the extension of BC; DE is the slanted line from D to E. Therefore, triangle DCE is a right triangle at C. Reasoning: The side length of the square is AB=8 cm, so BC=CD=8 cm. Also CE=2 cm, so the two right-angle sides of triangle DCE are DC=8 cm and CE=2 cm. Point P moves along A→B→C→D→A, with speed 2 cm/s. To make triangle PBC congruent to triangle DCE, the fixed side BC=8 cm must correspond to DC=8 cm, and the other side perpendicular to BC should be 2 cm. First case: when P is on AB, triangle PBC is a right triangle at B, and BP=CE=2 cm is needed. At this time AP=AB-BP=8-2=6 cm, and time t=6÷2=3 s. Second case: when P is on CD, triangle PBC is a right triangle at C, and CP=CE=2 cm is needed. At this time point P has already traveled AB+BC+CP=8+8+2=18 cm, and time t=18÷2=9 s. When P is on BC, the triangle degenerates, and when P is on DA, it cannot form the required 2 cm right-angle side. Therefore t=3 or 9.
